question: Identify, from the following, the moment used as a measure of skewness?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Third moment**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first moment** is called the **MEAN** which describes the center of the distribution.
 
• The **second moment** is the **VARIANCE** which describes the spread of the observations around the center.
 
• The **third moment** describes other aspects of a distribution such as how the distribution is skewed from its mean or peaked.
 
• **Skewness** is a measure of the asymmetry of a probability distribution about its mean.
 
• The third moment is often used as a measure of skewness, as it indicates the degree of asymmetry of a distribution.
 
• A **positive third moment **indicates that the distribution is skewed to the right, while a negative third moment indicates that the distribution is skewed to the left.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Skewness is a measure of the asymmetry of a distribution
 
• Third moment is used as a measure of skewness
 
• **Positive third moment** indicates a right-skewed distribution
 
• **Negative third moment **indicates a left-skewed distribution
 
• Other measures of skewness include the mean deviation and the coefficient of mean deviation.
 
• The third moment should be used with caution as it can be sensitive to outliers, and may not always accurately reflect the shape of a distribution. 
 
 
• It is important to consider the overall shape of a distribution and use multiple measures of skewness when analyzing data.
